author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
Unblocks #1956, the `@bfra.me/eslint-config` bump to `0.52.1`.

That release enables `unicorn/consistent-function-scoping`, which produces exactly one error across the repo:

```
77:5  error  Move function 'NullContextWrapper' to the outer scope  unicorn/consistent-function-scoping
✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
```

`NullContextWrapper` provides `value={null}` to exercise the null-context branch of `useTheme`'s guard. It references only the module-level `ThemeContext` import and its own `children` prop, so nothing tied it to the test that declared it.

## Why the other wrappers stay put

`packages/theme/test/theme-hooks.test.tsx` has four inner wrappers. Only this one is flagged, and that is correct — the other three each capture a context value constructed inside their own test:

| Wrapper | Captures | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NullContextWrapper` | nothing | hoisted |
| `CustomWrapper` | `contextValueWithMockSetTheme` | unchanged |
| `LoadingWrapper` | `loadingContextValue` | unchanged |
| `ErrorWrapper` | `errorContextValue` | unchanged |

Hoisting any of the other three would require lifting their context values to module scope too, which would leak per-test state across tests. The rule is right to leave them alone.

## Verification

Checked against the real `0.52.1` config in an isolated worktree, since the rule does not exist in the version currently on `main`:

- **Control** — original file reproduces the CI error exactly: `77:5 ... 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)`
- **After** — `npx eslint .` across the whole repo exits `0`
- `pnpm --filter @sparkle/theme test` — 8 files, 164 tests passing

The control run matters here: an earlier attempt to force the rule on without the plugin installed produced a misleading exit `0` because the rule never actually ran.
